summary: In SAPI CGI (php-cgi), a query string without the '=' character is treated as PHP command-line arguments. The attacker passes options such as -d auto_prepend_file=… and achieves arbitrary PHP code execution. Exploitable only when PHP runs as CGI under mod_cgi; mod_php and php-fpm are not affected.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Official images use mod_php (Apache) or php-fpm (nginx/alpine); the php-cgi mode is not used — NOT applicable to standard images; relevant only for custom builds with PHP-CGI.
Same: mod_php in the image, CGI mode is not used.

impact: Remote execution of arbitrary PHP code without authentication on PHP-CGI servers; massively exploited in 2012 (KEV).

public_poc.notes: Metasploit module php_cgi_arg_injection; also exploit-db 18834. KEV (CISA).

component_version_range: OpenSSL 1.0.1–1.0.1f (and 1.0.2-beta); outside the 2016–2026 window, but see notes
summary: Heartbleed: missing length validation in the TLS heartbeat extension allows remote reading of up to 64 KB of process memory (private keys, sessions, passwords). Outside the main window (2014), but Zabbix 3.0 images from 2016 could carry OpenSSL 1.0.1e/f — flagged as a historical check.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected in 2016 if the server had not been updated since April 2014; all distributions released patches. In practice: verify the actual libssl version on the target.

impact: Leak of up to 64 KB of TLS server process memory per request (private keys, credentials). KEV.

public_poc.notes: Metasploit openssl_heartbleed and dozens of PoCs.

summary: Several use-after-free bugs in ext/date (php_date.c): parsing serialized data with 'R'/'r' types (DateTimeZone/DateInterval) in unserialize() lets an attacker read memory or execute arbitrary code. The classic 2015 'PHP unserialize RCE'.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected (5.4.16/5.5.9/5.6 in the images); RHEL/Ubuntu/Alpine backport fixes — the actual package version needs fact-checking. The entry point is unserialize() with attacker-controlled data; the Zabbix frontend does not pass user data directly to unserialize → real reachability is low.
Same: nominally affected, distro backport.

impact: RCE (or memory disclosure) if the application has an unserialize() entry point with attacker-controlled data.

public_poc.notes: HackerOne report with PoC (ryat); public exploits from 2015; no ready-made Metasploit module.

summary: Padding oracle in the AES-NI CBC implementation: the implementation does not account for memory allocation while validating padding, allowing part of TLS traffic to be decrypted. Practical exploitation is difficult (requires an oracle and a large number of requests); no ready-made public exploits.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected until the patch (released May 2016); hard to exploit.

impact: Partial decryption of TLS traffic (conditional, high difficulty).

summary: Use-after-free in statem/statem.c after realloc with large TLS message sizes → DoS or possible code execution. Affects only OpenSSL 1.1.0a (September 2016); Zabbix 2016–2017 images used 1.0.1/1.0.2 → practically not applicable.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: 1.0.1/1.0.2 are not affected; 1.1.0a appeared only in the very latest builds of autumn 2016 — in practice not applicable to Zabbix images.

impact: DoS / potential RCE (1.1.0a only).

summary: Via MySQL logging functionality (or FILE privileges), an attacker writes a string into the my.cnf configuration file that makes mysqld load arbitrary code on the next restart → RCE with root/mysql privileges. Requires administrative or DB FILE privileges (post-exploitation or SQLi).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affected before the patch (5.7.16+/5.6.34+/5.5.53+); mysql images from Docker Hub get updated. Vector — FILE/admin access to the DB (usually after compromising an account or via SQLi).
Same (5.7 ≤5.7.15 affected).

impact: Remote RCE as root (config write → code execution on mysqld restart); local mysql→root escalation.

public_poc.notes: exploit-db 40360 (dawidgolunski); Metasploit modules; also affects MariaDB/Percona.

summary: Race condition when creating temporary tables (CREATE TEMPORARY): a local user with table-creation privileges swaps a tmp file with a symlink to an arbitrary file → privilege escalation to the system mysql user (and further to root via the 6662 chain).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affected before the patch; local vector — requires OS access under an account with the CREATE TEMPORARY privilege in the DB (e.g., the Zabbix account after its compromise).
Same.

impact: Privilege escalation (DB user → system mysql user → root).

summary: In <FilesMatch> expressions, the '$' character also matches a newline within the file name: a name like 'shell.php%0a' bypasses file-type restrictions. The classic file-upload restriction bypass (uploading and executing .php where it is forbidden).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally 2.4.6/2.4.7 < 2.4.29 — affected; RHEL/Ubuntu backport fixes. Requires a <FilesMatch> configuration and a file-upload mechanism; the Zabbix frontend has no file uploads with such a restriction → low applicability.
2.4.29 is within the range; Ubuntu backport. Applicability to Zabbix is low (no upload mechanism).

impact: Access control bypass and upload/execution of arbitrary files in vulnerable applications using <FilesMatch>.

public_poc.notes: The technique is publicly known (curl upload with a name ending in \n); no canonical PoC repository recorded.

summary: Carry propagation bug in Montgomery multiplication on x86_64: RSA operations with malformed input may crash or produce incorrect cryptographic results. Practical exploitation is difficult.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally in range before the patch; low practical significance.

impact: DoS / incorrect results of cryptographic operations (RSA).

summary: Integer overflow in the range filter module: a specially crafted Range request makes nginx return data outside the requested range (including cache file headers and contents, and adjacent memory areas). Remote disclosure of sensitive data.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: In range (≤1.13.2) → nominally affected; alpine backports fixes. Disclosure of the nginx frontend cache/memory.
Same (in range).
Out of range (1.16 > 1.13.2) → not affected.

impact: Information disclosure: reading fragments of nginx process memory / other responses from cache.

public_poc.notes: Well-known PoC scripts (gist/Python); mass scanning in 2017.

summary: Search_path hijack: a user with CREATE privilege on a schema (usually public) can replace functions/operators that privileged users and utilities (pg_dump, etc.) call without full qualification. Leads to code execution as the DB superuser.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affected before the patch; postgres images from Docker Hub get updated — recent tags are patched. The vector requires a DB account with CREATE on the public schema; the dedicated Zabbix user usually lacks such rights → low applicability for an external attacker; relevant in multi-tenant use of the DB server.
Same.

impact: Privilege escalation in the DB → code execution as superuser (via privileged utilities/applications).

public_poc.notes: Technique documented (A Guide to CVE-2018-1058); no ready-made 'out-of-the-box' exploits.

summary: UW IMAP Toolkit (used by imap_open() in PHP) runs rsh without argument escaping: a mailbox name with argument injection leads to OS command execution. Requires the php-imap extension and passing user input to imap_open().

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Conditional: only if the image has php-imap enabled AND the application calls imap_open() with user input. The Zabbix frontend does not use IMAP (media types are SMTP/scripts) → low applicability; verify whether the extension is actually present on the target.
Same condition (php-imap + an imap_open call).

impact: Remote command execution on the server if a vulnerable imap_open() call exists.

summary: Local privilege escalation to root: code running in less privileged child processes/threads (e.g., PHP via mod_php) can exploit a race in the scoreboard to overwrite the parent process memory and execute code as root. In KEV.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: 2.4.29 is within 2.4.17-2.4.38 → nominally affected (Ubuntu backport). Local vector: requires prior code execution as the apache user.
Same; focal (2.4.41) and centos7 (2.4.6) are out of range.

impact: Escalation to root on the server if code can be executed in the apache user context (e.g., via a PHP vulnerability or mod_cgi).

summary: Stack-based buffer overflow: any authenticated user can overflow the stack by changing their own password to a specially crafted value (SCRAM). Leads to a server crash, potentially to code execution in the postgres process context.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affected (10.x <10.9, 11.x <11.4); any authenticated DB user (including the Zabbix account after compromise) can trigger a crash/potential RCE.
Same for the PG 10/11 used.

impact: DoS (server crash) or code execution in the DB server context by an authenticated user.

summary: Underflow in php-fpm PATH_INFO handling: with a typical nginx+php-fpm configuration (fastcgi_split_path_info), FPM writes past the buffer into the FCGI protocol data area. Allows remote arbitrary code execution without authentication. Massively exploited (including in 2021); in KEV.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Zabbix nginx images use nginx+php-fpm with the typical location ~ \.php$ and fastcgi_split_path_info → affected when PHP <7.2.24 (before the alpine distro patch).
Affected when PHP <7.3.11; later 5.0.x on alpine 3.12/3.13 with PHP 7.4 — not affected.
httpd+mod_php variants are not affected (only php-fpm is vulnerable); relevant for nginx builds.

impact: Full remote RCE (code execution as the php-fpm user) without authentication on nginx+php-fpm servers.

public_poc.notes: phuip-fpizdam (neex) — a working exploit; mass exploitation, KEV (CISA).

summary: The DirectoryIterator class accepts file names containing an embedded \0 byte and truncates the name at that byte. This allows bypassing path checks in applications that restrict the directories accessible (info disclosure / access control bypass).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected (7.2/7.3 in bionic/centos8/alpine images); the Zabbix frontend does not use DirectoryIterator with user-supplied names for path checks → low practical significance.

impact: Bypass of file access restrictions (file disclosure) — depends on application logic.

summary: Buffer overread when parsing image EXIF data (exif_read_data()): a specially crafted image leads to memory content disclosure or a crash. Requires the exif extension and processing of user-supplied images.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Conditional: requires the exif extension and calls to exif_read_data() on user images; the Zabbix frontend does not parse EXIF images → low significance.

impact: Information disclosure (memory read) / DoS in applications parsing EXIF of user images.

summary: HTTP/2 'Data Dribble' attack: stream window manipulations force the worker to hold a large amount of data in small chunks → resource exhaustion (CPU/memory). DoS only.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected; HTTP/2 in Zabbix images is enabled only when TLS is configured (by default the frontend listens on HTTP:8080) → conditional. DoS — outside the main scope.

impact: Denial of service (exhaustion of nginx worker resources).

public_poc.notes: Techniques described in the advisory; no public PoC exploits.

summary: HTTP/2 'Resource Loop' attack: continuous reordering of stream priorities makes the server endlessly recompute priorities → CPU exhaustion. DoS only.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Same as CVE-2019-9511: nominally affected, HTTP/2 is enabled only with TLS → conditional.

impact: Denial of service (CPU exhaustion).

summary: A user with the right to create non-temporary objects in at least one schema can execute arbitrary code: malicious objects are picked up by privileged operations (related to CVE-2018-1058, search_path lookup during function execution).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affected before the patch; vector — a DB user with CREATE on a schema; applicability is low for the dedicated Zabbix DB.
Same.

impact: Arbitrary code execution as the DB superuser (given CREATE rights on a schema).

summary: Off-by-one in the nginx DNS resolver: an attacker able to spoof UDP responses from the DNS server triggers a 1-byte ('.') write past a heap buffer → worker crash or potentially more serious consequences. Requires resolver + proxy_pass with a variable.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: In range; but Zabbix nginx images use the resolver only with proxy_pass with a variable (not a typical config) → conditional.
1.16-1.20 is within the range up to 1.20.1 → nominally affected when the resolver is used; fixed in 1.20.1/1.21.0.

impact: Worker crash (DoS); potential RCE (not publicly confirmed).

public_poc.notes: X41 advisory with analysis; no public RCE exploit.

summary: Path normalization flaw in httpd 2.4.49: URL-encoded '../' bypasses Alias restrictions and reads files outside permitted directories; RCE is possible with mod_cgi enabled. Massively exploited in October 2021 (KEV).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Official Zabbix images do NOT contain httpd 2.4.49 (2.4.6/2.4.7/2.4.29/2.4.37/2.4.41/2.4.52/2.4.58). Applicable only to custom images built on distributions with 2.4.49 (e.g., Ubuntu 21.10).

impact: LFI (arbitrary file reading, including /etc/passwd) → RCE with mod_cgi enabled.

summary: The CVE-2021-41773 fix in 2.4.50 turned out incomplete: double URL-encoding ('%%32%65') again bypasses path normalization. Same path traversal; RCE with mod_cgi. KEV.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Official Zabbix images do not contain 2.4.49/2.4.50 → not applicable; relevant for custom builds of the specified versions.

impact: LFI → RCE (with mod_cgi) / arbitrary file reading.

summary: Buffer overflow in the mod_lua multipart parser (r:parsebody()) with a carefully crafted request body → potential RCE. Requires mod_lua to be loaded.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: mod_lua is not used in official Zabbix images → NOT applicable. Included for completeness of the Apache CVE list.

impact: DoS; potential RCE only with mod_lua enabled (Apache did not confirm exploitation).

public_poc.notes: No public PoC published (per Apache's statement).

summary: 4-byte overflow during name constraint checking of X.509 certificates with punycode email addresses. Triggered after chain signature verification: requires a certificate from a signing CA or an application that continues verification after a chain-building error. Crash or potential code execution.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: 3.0.2 is in range (≤3.0.6) → nominally affected; Ubuntu backports fixes (3.0.2-0ubuntu1.x). Noble (3.0.13) and focal (1.1.1) are not affected (fix in 3.0.7; the 1.1.1 branch is not vulnerable).

impact: Crash (DoS) when processing a malicious certificate; RCE not publicly confirmed.

public_poc.notes: Crash PoC only; no RCE exploit.

component_version_range: 3.0.0–3.0.6 (X.509, email addresses with a long punycode suffix)
summary: Buffer overflow when parsing email addresses with a long punycode suffix in X.509 certificates (in name constraint checking). Conditions are the same as CVE-2022-3602; leads to a crash or potentially code execution.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected before the backport; noble (3.0.13) not affected.

impact: Crash (DoS); potential RCE (not confirmed).

summary: Type confusion when processing X.400 addresses in X.509 GeneralName: the field is parsed as ASN1_STRING while the structure expects a different type → memory corruption during certificate name checking. Crash or potential RCE when processing a malicious certificate with X.400 addresses.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected before the backport; noble (3.0.13) and focal (1.1.1f with backport) — check the package version.
1.1.1 <1.1.1t nominally affected; distro backport.

impact: Crash (DoS) or potential RCE when checking a malicious certificate (X.400).

component_version_range: httpd 2.4.0–2.4.55 (mod_proxy + RewriteRule/ProxyPassMatch with a non-specific pattern)
summary: HTTP Request Smuggling in mod_proxy: when mod_proxy is configured together with RewriteRule/ProxyPassMatch with a non-specific pattern, the attacker injects a second request into the backend connection. Consequences — cache poisoning, ACL bypass, potentially RCE on the backend.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Zabbix images do not use mod_proxy by default (the frontend is served directly via mod_php/php-fpm). Conditionally applicable if the Zabbix frontend is proxied through httpd with mod_proxy.

impact: Request smuggling → cache poisoning, ACL bypass, potentially RCE on the proxied backend.

public_poc.notes: Several GitHub PoCs (dhmosfunk and others), packetstorm.

summary: Memory disclosure: calls to aggregate functions with 'unknown'-type arguments let a remote user read fragments of server memory (leftovers from previous queries). Requires DB access.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affected before the patch; requires DB access (SELECT on aggregates with unknown arguments).

impact: Information disclosure (fragments of DB server memory) by an authenticated user.

summary: Integer overflow when modifying SQL array values: missing overflow checks allow an authenticated user to trigger memory corruption and execute arbitrary code in the DB server context.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affected before the patch; vector — an authenticated DB user (the Zabbix account after compromise).

impact: Arbitrary code execution in the postgres process context by an authenticated DB user.

summary: Late privilege drop in REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY: the creator of a materialized view can execute arbitrary SQL functions as the user who ran the command (usually more privileged). Privilege escalation in the DB.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affected before the patch (16.2/15.6/14.11/13.14/12.18); requires the right to create materialized views — the dedicated Zabbix user usually lacks it → conditional.
Same.

impact: Execution of arbitrary SQL functions as a more privileged user (priv-esc in the DB).

summary: Improper control of environment variables in PL/Perl: an unprivileged DB user can modify sensitive environment variables (e.g., PATH) in the server process — often enough for arbitrary code execution. Requires the plperl extension installed.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected; requires the plperl extension enabled, which Zabbix does not use → low applicability; verify whether plperl is actually present on the target.

impact: Arbitrary code execution in the DB server context (if plperl is present).

summary: Bug in the convert.quoted-printable-decode stream filter (php://filter): processing certain data causes a 1-byte buffer overread — a crash or disclosure of adjacent memory areas is possible. Not a direct RCE.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected (8.3 < 8.3.14); Ubuntu/Alpine backport fixes — check the actual package version (e.g., php8.3-8.3.6-0ubuntu…). Low practical significance (1-byte overread).
Same: nominally 8.1 < 8.1.31, distro backport.

impact: Disclosure of 1 byte of memory / process crash when user data is processed by the quoted-printable filter.

summary: iconv() in glibc overflows the output buffer by up to 4 bytes when converting strings to the ISO-2022-CN-EXT encoding. In PHP applications (iconv/mbstring on user data) this becomes an RCE primitive; used in real exploitation chains in 2024.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: All glibc distributions ≤2.39 are affected before the patch; the Zabbix frontend does not convert user input via iconv to ISO-2022-CN-EXT → low applicability, but high profile when chained with other bugs.
Same.
Affected before the backport (2.39-0ubuntu8.3+).
Nominally affected; Alpine (musl) not affected.

impact: RCE/crash in applications converting user strings via iconv (PHP iconv/mbstring); up to 4 bytes of overflow.

public_poc.notes: Analysis and PoC by cfreal (Ambionics); used in RCE chains against PHP applications.

summary: SSRF in Apache HTTP Server on Windows: UNC path handling lets an attacker make the server contact an attacker-controlled host and leak NTLM hashes. Affects the Windows platform only.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Windows-only → NOT applicable to Zabbix Linux images. Included for completeness of the 2024 Apache summer series.

impact: SSRF and NTLM hash leakage (Windows deployments).

summary: Substitution encoding flaw in mod_rewrite: an attacker can execute scripts in directories permitted by the configuration but not directly reachable via URL, or obtain the source code of scripts that should only be executed → RCE/source disclosure.

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally in range (≤2.4.59); Ubuntu backports fixes — check the apache2 package version. Requires mod_rewrite with RewriteRule (the images contain a typical RewriteRule for /zabbix).
Same, nominally affected before the backport.
Same (2.4.58 ≤ 2.4.59), Ubuntu backport.

impact: Execution of scripts outside direct URL reach / source code disclosure → RCE in typical mod_rewrite configurations.

public_poc.notes: No public PoC found; exploitability depends on the RewriteRule configuration.

summary: Insufficient output escaping in mod_rewrite: an attacker maps URLs to file locations the server is allowed to serve but that are not intended for direct access → source code disclosure and potential script execution. In KEV (exploited in the wild).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected (≤2.4.59), Ubuntu backport; KEV — prioritize checking the actual apache2 version.
Same.
Same.

impact: Source code disclosure / RCE; exploited in the wild (KEV).

public_poc.notes: In KEV (CISA) — real-world exploitation; no public PoC repository found.

summary: Flaw in the httpd core: a backend application with malicious/exploitable response headers can lead to information disclosure, SSRF, or local script execution (processing of response headers from proxied applications).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Nominally affected (≤2.4.59), Ubuntu backport; the vector requires proxying a backend application with attacker-controlled headers — conditional for Zabbix.
Same.
Same.

impact: Info disclosure / SSRF / local script execution via backend response headers.

summary: On Windows, when running PHP-CGI under Apache on systems with certain code pages (Chinese/Japanese), the 'Best-Fit' mechanism substitutes characters in Win32 function command lines, letting the attacker inject PHP command-line arguments (similar to CVE-2012-1823). Remote code execution. Massively exploited in June 2024 (KEV).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Linux environments (all official Zabbix docker images) are NOT affected. Applicable only to non-standard Zabbix deployments on Windows with PHP-CGI.

impact: Full remote RCE without authentication on Windows servers with PHP-CGI; mass exploitation (KEV).

public_poc.notes: WatchTowr analysis and PoC; numerous GitHub PoCs; KEV (CISA).

summary: libpq escaping functions (PQescapeLiteral, PQescapeIdentifier, PQescapeString, PQescapeStringConn) do not neutralize quotes in input that has not passed encoding validation: the data provider can achieve SQL injection in applications using these functions (with certain client_encoding settings).

applies_to_zabbix.notes: Affects libpq client libraries (php-pgsql on Ubuntu uses libpq; psql). The Zabbix frontend builds queries in a parameterized way and does not use PQescape* with user input → low applicability; relevant for third-party applications on the same stack.

impact: SQL injection in applications using PQescape* on user data (requires specific client_encoding/invalid bytes).

public_poc.notes: Discussions and write-ups exist; no ready-made public exploit.
